html:
The Aswan High Dam is a huge rock and clay dam across the Nile at Aswan in southern Egypt, built from 1960 to 1970. It ended the river's yearly flood, which had shaped Egyptian farming since the pharaohs.

Nasser made the dam the symbol of his new Egypt. When the United States and Britain withdrew their offer of loans in 1956, he nationalised the Suez Canal Company to pay for it, and the Soviet Union stepped in with money and engineers.

  • Water stored behind it lets farmers grow two or three crops a year and protects Egypt from floods and droughts.
  • Its turbines once supplied about half of Egypt's electricity.
  • It made Lake Nasser, one of the largest artificial lakes in the world, stretching into Sudan.

The costs were real. Some 100,000 Nubians lost their homes, and UNESCO moved the temples of Abu Simbel to higher ground. The silt that fed the fields now settles in the lake, so farmers rely on fertiliser, and the Delta coast is wearing away.
